simulator_description: This simulator generates discrete-time stochastic COVID-style SIR epidemic trajectories, evolving integer counts of Susceptible (S), Infected (I), and Recovered (R) for a fixed population N over time. Each step samples new infections from a binomial draw with probability derived from a standard mass-action force of infection (1-exp(-beta*I/N)) and new recoveries from a binomial draw with rate gamma, then enforces nonnegativity and exact conservation S+I+R=N, which matches the closed-population SIR assumption used by the provided datasets. Calibration is done by simulating many candidate (beta, gamma) pairs from bounded priors and selecting those whose flattened raw-count trajectories best match a single observed training trajectory (trajectory_id=0), then using the best candidates as pseudo-posterior samples; evaluation sensibly averages multiple stochastic rollouts (and optionally multiple posterior thetas) to produce mean predicted trajectories and compute MSE and conservation-violation metrics.
